question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x},$ and simplify:

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{x}} &= \[5pt]
\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{x}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}} &= \[5pt]
\dfrac{x(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}) }{(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{x})(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x})} &= \[5pt]
\dfrac{x(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}) }{(\sqrt{2})^2-(\sqrt{x})^2} &= \[5pt]
\dfrac{x(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{x}) }{2-x} 
	}
$$
